translationRepairs: Gaozong personally brought the great enterprise to completion, and his merit and virtue were abundant. He ought therefore to be received as an associated sacrifice, following the precedent of our forebears, in keeping with the ancient scholars' insistence on revering the founding ancestor, and to manifest the martial founder's glory in sharing Heaven's sacrifice."

Gaozong personally brought the great enterprise to completion, and his merit and virtue were abundant. He ought therefore to be received as an associated sacrifice, following the precedent of our forebears, in keeping with the ancient scholars' insistence on revering the founding ancestor, and to manifest the accomplished ancestor's glory in sharing Heaven's sacrifice."
文祖 is the cultured/accomplished ancestor, not a martial founder.

By the Shaoxing period (1131–1162) music was restored. To honor the sacred ceremonial headdress, an edict forbade female performers among the color-bearing musicians and directed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to station the musicians outside the gate only.

By the Shaoxing period (1131–1162) music was restored. To honor the empress's pheasant-patterned ceremonial robes, an edict forbade female performers among the color-bearing musicians and directed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to station the musicians outside the gate only.
禕翟 are the empress's pheasant robes, not a headdress.

The suburban sacrifice is a weighty affair: its musicians attend the imperial carriage in person and perform the elegant harmonies, expected to link Heaven and earth and honor the ancestors. I beg that their daily provisions be increased, paid from the memorial-field office treasury, so that their skill may gradually improve, with rewards and encouragement added besides.

The suburban sacrifice is a weighty affair: its musicians attend the imperial carriage in person and perform the elegant harmonies, expected to link Heaven and earth and honor the ancestors. I beg that their daily provisions be increased, paid from the treasury of the Office of the Sacred Field, so that their skill may gradually improve, with rewards and encouragement added besides.
籍田司 is the office of the emperor's ploughing field.

When Ningzong ascended the throne, Xiaozong was enshrined in the main temple line, Xizu was moved to a separate temple, and a dedicated shrine was established. The ritual officers submitted: "Xizu, having been established as a separate temple on the Tang model of Xingsheng, is sacrificed at his own shrine when the collapse rite is performed. On the mid-winter day of the collapse sacrifice, rites should first be conducted at Xizu's temple chamber.

When Ningzong ascended the throne, Xiaozong was enshrined in the main temple line, Xizu was moved to a separate temple, and a dedicated shrine was established. The ritual officers submitted: "Xizu, having been established as a separate temple on the Tang model of Xingsheng, is sacrificed at his own shrine when the joint ancestral rite is performed. On the mid-winter day of the joint ancestral sacrifice, rites should first be conducted at Xizu's temple chamber.
祫 is the joint ancestral sacrifice, not a collapse rite.

Then the officials submitted: "On the Double Ninth holy day the emperor went to Shoukang Palace to offer longevity wishes and perform music—embodying the retired sovereign's utmost filial devotion to his parent, and fulfilling his subjects' reverence toward ruler and parent alike. This is among the greatest ceremonial norms of the state.

Then the officials submitted: "On the Chongming Sage Festival (the retired emperor's birthday) the emperor went to Shoukang Palace to offer longevity wishes and perform music—embodying the sage ruler's utmost filial devotion to his parent, and fulfilling his subjects' reverence toward ruler and parent alike. This is among the greatest ceremonial norms of the state.
重明聖節 is Guangzong's birthday festival, not Double Ninth; 聖主 is the reigning emperor.
According to precedent, on the Heavenly Application festival the imperial banquet was granted on the day following the longevity offering.
According to precedent, on the Tianshen Festival (Gaozong's birthday) the imperial banquet was granted on the day following the longevity offering.
天申節 is a named birthday festival, not a literal phrase.

By the fourteenth year (1222), an edict proclaimed: "Cities of Shandong and Hebei, moved by our righteousness, and foreign peoples submitting at the suburban sacrifice, have presented jade and treasure as tribute. The inscription reads 'The Emperor Respectfully Receives the Mandate of Heaven Treasure'—truly an heirloom of our ancestors."

By the fourteenth year of Jiading (1221), an edict proclaimed: "Cities of Shandong and Hebei, moved by our righteousness, and foreign peoples submitting at the suburban sacrifice, have presented jade and treasure as tribute. The inscription reads 'The Emperor Respectfully Receives the Mandate of Heaven Treasure'—truly an heirloom of our ancestors."
Only when presenting the register and seal to Empress Dowager Shou Mingren Fuci Ruishou were new musical pieces composed for the ceremony.
Only when presenting the register and seal to Empress Dowager Shouming Renfu Cirui were new musical pieces composed for the ceremony.
壽明仁福慈睿 is misdivided and adds a spurious 'shou'.

Gong is the husband and zhi the wife; though shang is gong's parent tone, it is in fact zhi's child—by having the wife assist the husband and the son assist the mother, the tones then form a coherent pattern.

Gong is the husband and zhi the wife; though shang is fathered by gong, it is in fact zhi's child—by having the wife assist the husband and the son assist the mother, the tones then form a coherent pattern.
商雖父宮 means gong is shang's father, not the reverse.
Only the pieces "Yingfu" and "Offering Immortal Music" are termed courtly pieces (fayue); these are the Tang dynasty's courtly music department.
Only the pieces "Yingfu" and "Offering Immortal Music" are termed courtly pieces (faqu); these are the Tang dynasty's courtly music department.
法曲 is read faqu, not fayue.
"The king's great feasts, with three libations."
"The king's great feasts, with music played three times to urge the meal."
侑 here is urging food with music, not libations.
All other private variations in pitch or quantity should be forbidden; then the people will "follow the emperor's standard," and customs may be set right.
All other private variations in pitch or quantity should be forbidden; then the people will "follow the pattern of God on High," and customs may be set right.
順帝之則 quotes the Shijing; 帝 is the high god.
The six lü in performance are yang-dominant; the six lü in song are yin-dominant—the timbres differ yet their virtue harmonizes. This principle has been lost since the Tang.
The six lü in performance are yang-dominant; the six yin pitches (lü 呂) in song are yin-dominant—the timbres differ yet their virtue harmonizes. This principle has been lost since the Tang.
律 and 呂 are conflated in the English.

Kui then composed the "Holy Song Nao Songs" himself: "Heaven's Command" for the Song receiving the Mandate, "Beyond the River" for pacifying Shangdang, "Huaihai Turbid" for securing Weiyang, "Above the Yuan" for taking Hunan, "Imperial Might Unfettered" for obtaining Jingzhou, "Shu Mountains Deep" for conquering Shu, "Seasonal Rain Abundant" for taking Guangnan, "Gazing at Zhong Mountain" for subduing Jiangnan, "How Great the Benevolence" for Wu and Yue's submission, "Songs of Praise Return" for Zhang and Quan's offering of territory, "Merit of Campaign Continued" for conquering Hedong, "The Emperor Approaches the Rampart" for the Chanyuan campaign, "Sustaining Four Generations" praising benevolent rule, and "Blazing Essence Restored" celebrating the restoration—fourteen pieces in all, submitted to the Ministry of Personnel.

Kui then composed the "Holy Song Nao Songs" himself: "Heaven's Command" for the Song receiving the Mandate, "Beyond the River" for pacifying Shangdang, "Huaihai Turbid" for securing Weiyang, "Above the Yuan" for taking Hunan, "Imperial Might Unfettered" for obtaining Jingzhou, "Shu Mountains Deep" for conquering Shu, "Seasonal Rain Abundant" for taking Guangnan, "Gazing at Zhong Mountain" for subduing Jiangnan, "How Great the Benevolence" for Wu and Yue's submission, "Songs of Praise Return" for Zhang and Quan's offering of territory, "Merit of Campaign Continued" for conquering Hedong, "The Emperor Approaches the Rampart" for the Chanyuan campaign, "Sustaining Four Generations" praising benevolent rule, and "Blazing Essence Restored" celebrating the restoration—fourteen pieces in all, submitted to the Department of State Affairs.
尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs, not the Ministry of Personnel (吏部).

At the Qingyuan Classics Lectures, Xi once drafted a memorial stating: "Since the Qin extinguished learning, ritual and music were the first to collapse, and music as a discipline has lacked any transmission from masters.

While lecturing at the Classics Mat in the Qingyuan era, Xi once drafted a memorial stating: "Since the Qin extinguished learning, ritual and music were the first to collapse, and music as a discipline has lacked any transmission from masters.
經筵 is the imperial Classics Mat; 慶元 is the era name.
Later, while compiling his Book of Rites, he established chapters on "Bell Standards" and "Music Institutions," leaving authoritative teachings for posterity.
Later, while compiling his ritual compendium, he established chapters on "Bell Standards" and "Music Institutions," leaving authoritative teachings for posterity.
禮書 is Zhu Xi's own ritual compilation, not the classic Book of Rites.

At the beginning of Jianlong, Wang Pu's music was adopted. The Founding Emperor, upon hearing it once, found it too high and uncomfortably mournful. He ordered He Ning to examine the Western Capital pitch measure and lower the pitch by one degree; compared with the previous music, it first became harmonious.
